page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL processor cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 262 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between compute performance and memory capacity. The server exhibits weak to poor CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% at 944.79 and multi-core scoring in the bottom 25% at 5438.12. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores also fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, memory subsystem performance is stable, with average ratings across memory bandwidth tests, including 365.97 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 42.22 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Passmark memory scores and database operations both rank in the middle 50%, alongside a Redis SET throughput of 6.25 million operations per second.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average database operation benchmarks, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and moderate data processing tasks. Conversely, it is poorly suited for compute-heavy applications, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference, as demonstrated by weak static web serving throughput and poor 7B model prompt processing.
